SPIKE RESULT: pass-through decoder works on HTTP, but the stream is only alive INSIDE Decode. That blocks the relay half of item 3, not the store half.

Verified empirically against real `git http-backend` (CGI, protocol v2), three tests:

1. PASS-THROUGH YIELDS THE RAW STREAM. `smartPackSession` does implement `transport.Commander`. `Command(ctx, "fetch", &packp.FetchArgs{...}, passthroughDecoder)` where Decode does `io.Copy(&buf, r)` captures the full v2 envelope byte-for-byte: `000dpackfile\n` + `\x01PACK\x00\x00\x00\x02...` + trailing `0006\x01\\` `0000`. Same shape git-sync's `PostRPCStreamBody` returns today, so `openV2PackStream`/`consumeV2FetchPack` would parse it unchanged.

2. THE READER IS DEAD ONCE Command RETURNS. `smartPackSession.Command` (handshake.go:276) ends with an unconditional `defer { io.Copy(io.Discard, r.resp.Body); r.resp.Body.Close() }` — the code comment says outright "Command consumes the whole response (it never streams the body out)". A decoder that reads one byte then stashes the reader gets `http: read on closed response body` afterwards. n=0.

   One trap worth knowing: if the decoder reads NOTHING, `r.resp` is still nil when the defer runs, because `httpRequester` fires the POST lazily on first Read. So a stashed reader appears to work — but the POST then executes after Command returned, outside its error handling. That's an accident, not a seam. My first cut of the test hit exactly this and gave a false pass.

3. RELAY INSIDE Decode WORKS END-TO-END. Command(fetch, decoder) → decoder strips the envelope → streams the demuxed pack into `git index-pack --stdin` in a second repo → source head resolves as a commit there. A slow external consumer is fine; nothing buffers the body.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR ITEM 3 — it splits cleanly in two:

  (a) `fetchToStoreV2` and `FetchCommitParents` are ALREADY callback-shaped — both run `consumer func(io.Reader) error` inside the call. These port to `Command` directly. Unblocked, I'll take them.

Those are packages your brief says to keep as-is.

MY CALL: do (a) now, hold (b). (b) is a behavior-preserving but wide refactor across three strategy packages for no security win — the two advisories were in shellQuotePath and the redirect credential re-attach, neither of which lives in the fetch relay path. - go-git does NOT tighten the in-flight redirect hop. checkRedirect's own doc comment says credential handling on redirect "is left to Go's http.Client". Go's rule is shouldCopyHeaderOnRedirect → idnaASCIIFromURL → url.Hostname(). Port stripped. Verified in the Go 1.26.6 source. So the stdlib forwards Authorization from host:443 to host:9999, and go-git adds nothing there. Routing fetch through Handshake would move that path OFF our guard and onto the weaker rule — a regression, not a fix, unless we pass our own client via Options.Client (resolveClient does preserve a caller's CheckRedirect, so that composes).

Options gives us Client, Authorizer, FollowRedirects, HTTPProxy, TLS, ForceDumb — and no retry seam.

Item 1 landed: commit 4ac28dfa. Session collapses a run's upload-pack RPCs onto one helper process. Per-RPC path confirmed intact — explicit test below.

THE FRAMING BLOCKER DOES NOT EXIST. I flagged it and you restated it, and we were both wrong. responseEndReader already has exactly the right semantics for a persistent session: fill() consumes the 0002 and sets done, leaving the underlying bufio positioned at the next byte. So one reader per response over a shared stream just works — no mode, no rewrite, zero lines changed in it. What I needed from it was the opposite of a change: `done` is the signal for whether a response completed, which is how the session knows if the wire is still trustworthy.

WHERE I DEVIATED FROM YOUR ROUTE, AND WHY
You asked for the capability interface AND for the cost to stay bounded to helper.go. Those pull apart: if refs.go and fetch.go type-assert, the branching lands in them, not helper.go, and every call site grows two paths.

Resolved by putting the assert at the conn lifecycle owner instead. syncer.go asserts once, right after building the source conn, and calls BeginV2Session; finish() already called sourceConn.Close(), which now ends it. refs.go and fetch.go are untouched — they still call RequestInfoRefs and PostRPCStreamBody, which route through the session internally when one is live. So you get your mechanism (narrow optional interface, only HelperConn implements it, type-assert with silent fallback) and your cost profile (two paths, both inside helper.go). 14 lines in syncer.go, and they are the assert plus its comment.

WHAT IT DOES
- V2SessionConn { BeginV2Session(ctx) error } in helper_session.go, documented as the Commander-style optional capability and saying why it is not part of Conn (SSHConn needs the dialer seam, HTTPConn is stateless — widening Conn forces two of three implementors to carry a method they cannot honour).
- RequestInfoRefs serves the cached advertisement on a live session; the helper emits it before its request loop, so it genuinely cannot be re-read.
- postSession does NOT close stdin. EncodeCommand already ends every body with a flush-pkt, which is exactly what the helper's ReadFlushTerminatedMessage waits for — I verified that rather than assuming it, since closing stdin would end the loop and throw the session away.
- The session steps aside whenever the wire position stops being known: receive-pack never rides it, and a response abandoned before its response-end drops the session. Both fall back to a fresh process, correctness over the saved round trip.

TESTS — added a "session" mode to the fake helper that loops like stateless.go:60, plus a spawn counter:
- ReusesOneProcess: advertisement + 2 commands = 1 spawn (was 3), responses byte-identical with 0002 stripped
- NoSession_StillOneProcessPerRPC: without BeginV2Session, 2 RPCs = 2 spawns. This is your explicit confirmation that the per-RPC path still passes with the session code in place.
- ReceivePackStillPerRPC: session live, push still gets its own process
- AbandonedResponseDropsSession: partial read + Close drops the session, next RPC still succeeds
- BeginIsIdempotent: 3 calls = 1 spawn
- CloseWithoutBegin

LOC: +236/−11 production (net +225), +213/−9 test. This one ADDS code — it is a process-lifetime win, not a deletion, and I did not use transport.NewStreamSession to get it. Using it would have meant re-encoding the capability advertisement back to bytes to satisfy RequestInfoRefs' []byte contract, or teeing the handshake and re-framing pkt-lines by hand — which is the code we are trying to delete. The go-git deletion on this path needs the caller-facing seam to move, i.e. the thing we agreed to defer. Flagging plainly so nobody reads this commit as go-git adoption.
